## Overview

You will take three quizzes during the term, given at the end of class on the Fridays of weeks 1, 2, and 3. Each quiz covers material from that week — both the textbook chapters and any assigned articles or class discussions. Together the quizzes count for **30%** of your final grade (10% each).

The quizzes serve two purposes: (1) they give you regular, low-stakes opportunities to check your comprehension of core IPE concepts, and (2) they build cumulatively toward the final exam.

## Schedule

| Quiz | Date | Coverage |
|------|------|----------|
| Quiz 1 | Friday, July 10 | Chapters 1–4 (Introduction; trade system; cooperation; society-centered trade) |
| Quiz 2 | Friday, July 17 | Chapters 5–9 (State-centered trade; ISI & neoliberalism combined; MNCs in the global economy; politics of MNCs) |
| Quiz 3 | Friday, July 24 | Chapters 10–13 (International monetary system; cooperation/conflict in the contemporary IMS; monetary politics — society-centered & state-centered) |

## Format

Each quiz is approximately **30 minutes**, taken at the end of class. Quizzes consist of:

- **Multiple-choice questions** testing recognition of key terms, concepts, and arguments from the readings
- **Short-answer questions** asking you to apply or compare frameworks from the chapters

You should expect questions on:

- Definitions and characteristics of major theoretical approaches
- Logic of key arguments in the chapters
- Evidence and examples used to support those arguments
- Application of frameworks to short scenarios

## Preparation

The most reliable way to prepare is to (1) complete each chapter carefully *before* class, (2) participate actively during the week's lectures and discussions, and (3) take the in-class writing prompts seriously — they are designed to deepen your understanding of core concepts and help you connect those concepts to current policy questions.


## Policies

- Quizzes are taken in class. They cannot be made up except in cases of documented absence cleared with the instructor in advance.
- Generative AI tools may not be used during quizzes.
- If accommodations are needed, please contact me and Disability Services for Students at the start of the term.
